### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, touching **3** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/environment-variables.mdx`  _(via OS_TRUSTED_APP_SCHEMES (literal, a string literal in TRUSTED_APP_SCHEMES_ENV_NAME))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `os serve (command, 46 pages)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **35** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0b99c2b1645b101459b1dd9fd4fecdf996194a76` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ce0dd3227535871d446ab8d1b7a0878cfbff35cd` — the merge of head `3b20bb01516dbf4ecca3667e713bc068fdefa1cf` into base `0b99c2b1645b101459b1dd9fd4fecdf996194a76`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ce0dd3227535871d446ab8d1b7a0878cfbff35cd && git checkout ce0dd3227535871d446ab8d1b7a0878cfbff35cd
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0b99c2b1645b101459b1dd9fd4fecdf996194a76 3b20bb01516dbf4ecca3667e713bc068fdefa1cf && git checkout -B drift-repro 0b99c2b1645b101459b1dd9fd4fecdf996194a76 && git merge --no-ff 3b20bb01516dbf4ecca3667e713bc068fdefa1cf

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0b99c2b1645b101459b1dd9fd4fecdf996194a76
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0b99c2b1645b101459b1dd9fd4fecdf996194a76` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `3b20bb01516dbf4ecca3667e713bc068fdefa1cf`
Local-runs: none

Face: declaration (`Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`). No published schema and no governed path in the committed tree (7 files). Read: the full diff, card #29972 and its triage audit 6614052196 (human floor: auth boundary), and the dev report at `/mnt/project-files/issue-29972/os-dev-report.md`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **One reader, the `OS_TRUSTED_ORIGINS` shape.** `resolveTrustedAppSchemes(process.env)` splits on `,`, trims, drops empties and folds repeats, and answers `undefined` when nothing is left. That value goes to `new AuthPlugin({ trustedAppSchemes })` beside `trustedOrigins`. Unset, empty, or separators only all stay unset: no default scheme, and the `one-time-token` plugin stays unmounted. That is the card's "unset stays unset", pinned in the contract test.
- **A bad entry still fails loudly.** The reader never validates, lower-cases or drops an entry. `assertTrustedAppSchemes` refuses a bad one at construction; the dev measured a live boot with `MyApp` exiting 1 and naming the entry. No silent drop: the ablation of a silently dropping reader goes red.
- **Every CLI door.** `serve.ts` is the only CLI site that builds `AuthPlugin`. `os dev` and `os start` spawn `serve` with the inherited environment, so one line covers all three. Measured, not assumed.
- **Live boot, as the card asked.** Set: the hand-off answers `401` without a session and `302` signed in. Unset: `400` "is not a registered app scheme". This is the card's acceptance pair.
- **Gate edits outside the claimed surface are mechanical.** `cross-package-test-inputs.mjs` and `turbo.json` name `environment-variables.mdx` as an input of `cli#test`, because the contract test reads that page's row. `check-ci-filter-parity`'s rollback pin moves 19 → 20, recorded by name. Accepted.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/cli`, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none` on PR body and changeset. `TRUSTED_APP_SCHEMES_ENV_NAME` and `resolveTrustedAppSchemes` are exported from `serve.ts` but not re-exported from the package entry, so the public surface does not move. No stack key is added (environment only, as ordered), and `AuthConfig.trustedAppSchemes` already exists in the spec. Correct.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Human floor (triage 6614052196):** this decides who may receive a sign-in hand-off. The PR states how the setting is read and that an unset value keeps the plugin unmounted. The maintainer reviews it before it lands, as on #29714. The seat does not arm automerge on its own ACCEPT.
- Out of scope, as the card says: the hosted runtime's own `AuthPlugin` (cloud lane, tracked from mobile#148).
- Author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`: no non-fleet login to name. Dev `open_questions`: none.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-p09liv`
Reviewed-by: `session_01WGufzibcN9oHa8kDbTTnL5`

**VERDICT: PASS**
